composition_answer: YES. The package is the complete and sufficient authorization component for exactly one future retained-only representative shared-expert recovery event: it pins the representative F_norm input (687a692a...), all three exact surface-independent model-weight authorities (27623424 packed bytes, packed and decoded hashes anchored to the completed canonical source event), the computation and output contracts, the executor identity, and one-shot semantics, and the committed executor can instantiate exactly one event (exclusive state and output roots, durable attempt-start and computation-start records, failure-after-attempt-start consumes the release, retry/resume/second-attempt false and mutation-enforced). By design it does not itself release execution: real_event_authorized is false, status is PREPARED_REVIEW_REQUIRED, and the executor structurally requires a future single-use release token binding the authorization sha256 with disposition GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY and real_event_authorized true, which must come from the separate independently approved release cycle. It authorizes zero checkpoint reads and zero shard opens (checkpoint fallback impossible), and it authorizes no routed/shared combination, no FFN completion, and no S2 construction: those are absent from the executor code, prohibited with validator-enforced true flags, pinned to zero in accounting, and the stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_SHARED_EXPERT_OUTPUT_ONLY is enforced and mutation-tested.

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The output contract states sha256_recorded_after_descriptor_readback true, but the executor records terminal output_sha256 via sha_file (a fresh open by path) after the no-replace hard-link publish rather than reading back from a descriptor-verified handle. The publish is O_EXCL temp + fsync + link + parent fsync into an output root the process just created exclusively, and every downstream consumer re-verifies by hash, so only a same-user local race could mis-record. Recommend the future release wrapper re-verify the published output identity from an fstat-checked descriptor or re-hash EXPECTED==PUBLISHED before banking.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: TERMINAL_OUTPUT_HASH_RECORDED_BY_PATH_REOPEN_NOT_DESCRIPTOR_READBACK

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: state_root and output_root are CLI-supplied; the executor enforces exclusivity per supplied root (PRIOR_EVENT_STATE, mkdir exist_ok False, O_EXCL attempt-start), but nothing in this package pins the single machine-wide attempt root. This matches the accepted routed-aggregate precedent where the single-use release wrapper pinned the exclusive roots. The future release package must pin exact state and output roots and bind the committed validator before invocation.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: MACHINE_WIDE_ONE_SHOT_EXCLUSIVITY_DEFERRED_TO_RELEASE_PACKAGE

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: execute() validates the document parsed in main() but computes sha_file(authorization_path) separately for the token binding and the attempt-start record, so a same-user local swap between parse and hash could make the recorded sha diverge from the parsed bytes. Not exploitable for substitution because validate_authorization pins every consequential field to committed constants (input sha, full parameter identity, accounting, prohibitions), so any passing document is semantically identical. Recommend hashing the exact bytes that were parsed.
defense_in_depth_findings.title: AUTHORIZATION_PARSED_ONCE_BUT_HASHED_SEPARATELY_IN_EXECUTE

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: CANONICAL_REPRESENTATIVE_POST_ATTENTION_FFN_NORMALIZED_SHARED_EXPERT_INPUT is defined only inside this package; upstream authorities bind the identical byte identity 687a692a... under CANONICAL_REPRESENTATIVE_POST_ATTENTION_FFN_NORMALIZED_EXPERT_INPUT (ffn-composition semantics, with shared_expert_input true) and stage name router_normalized (m1f0 stage vocabulary and real execution evidence). No consumable ambiguity exists because all bindings are by sha256 and the composition semantics contract proves shared and routed use the same F_norm, but the alias should be registered in the next vocabulary revision to keep the evidence vocabulary closed.

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: compute() and decode_parameters() carry a rehearsal-only disagreement_role keyword used to exercise the DUAL_DECODER_DISAGREEMENT failure path. It defaults to None, execute() never passes it, and no CLI plumbing reaches it, so the real event cannot be affected; the executor sha is pinned so it cannot drift silently. Cosmetic: a future executor revision could isolate fault injection in the rehearsal module.

statement: The committed representative shared-expert recovery authorization package is bound, executable, checkpoint-free, and correctly scoped. Every declarative sha256 pin recomputes byte-exact against committed bytes; the committed validator (repo mode) and all 6 committed unit tests (30 authorization mutations) pass; all 7 kernel/decoder implementation identities match live source; the representative input 687a692a... is byte-identically the banked m1f0 router_normalized stage output, which the frozen layer3 semantic graph v2 defines as F_norm (layer3_ffn_normalized_router_and_expert_input) feeding Route, Routed, and Shared, so it is the correct post-attention FFN-normalized shared-expert input and the historical direct-DPREFIX input surface is excluded by exact-hash pinning and enforced prohibitions; the three retained gate/up/down packed weights re-hash byte-exact (0400, nlink 1, regular, machine-local, paths withheld), their 27623424-byte inventory is arithmetically complete (Q5_K 49152x176 twice, Q6_K 49152x210) and complete by construction (the committed runtime map defines exactly three shexp tensors per layer), and both packed and decoded identities anchor to the independently reviewed canonical shared-expert recovery source event (ledger 163->166, 3 reads, 1 shard open); checkpoint access and fallback are structurally impossible (no checkpoint or shard interface in executor, validator, or rehearsal; access dicts pinned to zero and mutation-enforced); consume-what-you-validated holds via single-descriptor O_NOFOLLOW EXPECTED==BEFORE==CONSUMED==AFTER with nlink-1 and read-only gates (hard-link alias and writable alias independently verified rejected, closing prior-cycle D4/D5); the strict-f32 gate/up/SiLU/hadamard/down math, dtype and casting points, increasing-column order, and f32le[6144] 24576-byte output serialization match the frozen semantic graph exactly; this review independently reproduced the live real-retained preflight (PRODUCTION_BINDINGS_RESOLVED, all five after-hashes exact) and produced a third independent fresh-process synthetic computation on real retained weight bytes that byte-exactly reproduced the banked rehearsal output 9eb5ee8d..., confirming decoder and kernel executability end-to-end without computing the real event; the one-shot release gate fails closed (live-tested: a token without real_event_authorized true is rejected with FUTURE_SINGLE_USE_RELEASE_REQUIRED and zero durable writes); the stop boundary is enforced by absence (no routed, FFN, or S2 code path exists in the executor) and by validator-enforced prohibitions. No blocking or non-blocking-required findings; five defense-in-depth recommendations recorded for the future single-use release cycle.
